back2basics.text: The Election Commission of India is a constitutional body responsible for administering elections and maintaining electoral rolls. Article 324 of the Constitution grants it superintendence, direction, and control over elections. Electoral rolls are periodically revised to include eligible voters and remove ineligible ones, with processes like the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) aimed at updating voter lists comprehensively.

2026-10-15-am-5706b802cf.deck: A plea filed by Rahul Gandhi and opposition leaders challenges the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging irregularities and voter deletions. The Supreme Court has not yet listed the plea for hearing due to procedural defects, while political protests continue over the Election Commission's actions.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court petition on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls:
1. The petition alleges large-scale voter deletions and seeks suspension of the ongoing SIR.
2. The Chief Justice of India has refused to hear the petition citing lack of jurisdiction.
mcq.trap: The CJI has not refused to hear the petition but has deferred listing it until procedural defects are cured; the petition does allege voter deletions and seeks suspension of SIR.

body.label: Petition details
body.text: Rahul Gandhi and 10 opposition leaders filed a plea alleging large-scale voter deletions and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

body.label: Relief sought
body.text: The plea seeks suspension of the ongoing SIR, constitution of an independent audit committee headed by a retired apex court judge, and directions to ensure no elector is deleted without notice and hearing.

body.label: Parties involved
body.text: The Election Commission of India, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi are respondents in the case.

sections.heading: What is the Supreme Court petition about?

body.label: Procedural defects
body.text: The Supreme Court registry flagged 14 defects in the petition, including missing clear ID copies and illegible or missing pages, which have yet to be cured.

body.label: Court’s assurance
body.text: The Chief Justice of India assured that the matters will be listed for hearing once the defects are rectified.

body.label: Separation of powers
body.text: The CJI declined a request for a meeting to submit a memorandum, citing that addressing sub judice issues outside court would breach judicial propriety.

sections.heading: Why has the Supreme Court not heard the petition yet?

body.label: Article 324 powers
body.text: The petition questions whether decisions related to the SIR comply with Article 324, which vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission.

body.label: Statutory compliance
body.text: It challenges compliance with the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, and the Representation of the People Act, 1950.

body.label: Transparency demands
body.text: The plea demands publication of booth-wise deleted electors, reasons for deletions, and a mechanism to restore eligible voters.

sections.heading: What are the key legal and constitutional issues raised?

2026-10-15-am-eecd29b343.anchor: Social welfare schemes and vulnerable sections

back2basics.text: Social welfare schemes are government initiatives aimed at providing financial support and social security to vulnerable and marginalized populations. These schemes often include pensions, subsidies, and direct transfers to improve living conditions and reduce poverty. The National Social Assistance Programme is one such scheme providing pensions to elderly, widows, disabled persons, and families of deceased breadwinners, funded fully by the central government to ensure uniformity across states.

2026-10-15-am-eecd29b343.deck: The Union Cabinet approved the continuation of the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP) with a budget of ₹53,428 crore for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31, including renaming the scheme and revising eligibility and assistance for disability pensions. This matters for UPSC aspirants as it reflects government social welfare policy updates, budgetary allocations, and changes in scheme design affecting vulnerable populations.

mcq.stem: Consider the following statements about the National Social Assistance Programme (NSAP): 1. NSAP has been renamed as Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana with sub-schemes also renamed dropping the 'Indira Gandhi' prefix. 2. The eligibility for disability pension under NSAP has been revised to require a minimum 40% benchmark disability instead of 80%. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: A trap is confusing the previous 80% benchmark disability criterion with the revised 40% criterion; both statements are correct as per the Cabinet approval.

pyq.question: ‘Women’s movement in India has not addressed the issues of women of lower social strata.’ Substantiate your view.
pyq.why: The NSAP includes widow pension schemes, and changes in coverage and eligibility criteria highlight challenges faced by women of lower social strata in accessing social welfare, relevant to the question on women's movements addressing issues of marginalized women.

body.label: Scheme continuation and funding
body.text: NSAP will continue for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31 with a total outlay of ₹53,428 crore.

body.label: Renaming of scheme and sub-schemes
body.text: NSAP is renamed as Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana; old age, widow, disability, and family benefit schemes are renamed accordingly, dropping the 'Indira Gandhi' prefix.

body.label: Disability pension revisions
body.text: Eligibility for disability pension now requires 40% benchmark disability instead of 80%, with assistance rates of ₹375 for ages 0-79 and ₹625 for 80+, and minimum age criterion set since birth.

body.label: Other pension schemes
body.text: Pension schemes for old aged, widows, and family benefit will continue in their existing form.

sections.heading: What are the key changes approved for the National Social Assistance Programme?

body.label: Uniform central assistance
body.text: The scheme provides 100% central assistance to ensure uniform support to beneficiaries across all States and UTs.

body.label: Coverage and beneficiary impact
body.text: Approximately 3.20 crore beneficiaries across 36 States and UTs will benefit from the scheme continuation and revisions.

body.label: Criticism of fixed budget and coverage
body.text: Critics argue the fixed five-year budget does not account for rising beneficiary numbers or inflation, potentially limiting adequacy.

body.label: State-level pension schemes
body.text: Due to limited central coverage capped at 3.09 crore, many States run their own pension schemes, increasing total coverage to about 8.95 crore beneficiaries.

sections.heading: Why do these changes matter for social welfare and policy?

body.label: Launch and constitutional basis
body.text: NSAP was launched on 15 August 1995 to assist poor households under Article 41 of the Directive Principles of State Policy.

body.label: Rights of Persons with Disability Act 2016
body.text: The Act required linking disability pension eligibility to 40% benchmark disability and mandated disability assistance to be 25% higher than similar schemes.
